scientific limitations/integrity: The result concerns the strict primitive-abundant convention and exactly two distinct prime factors. The underlying factor classification is treated as classical: later full-text literature explicitly records Dickson’s 1913 coverage of all even primitive abundant numbers with at most three distinct prime factors. The assessed contribution is the exact counting identity and its log-periodic prime-number-theorem consequence. The infinite asymptotic is proved symbolically; the included finite computation is corroborative only. The full 1913 article text was not available line-by-line in the inspected open sources, so an obscure differently phrased historical counting result remains the principal originality risk.
title: A log-periodic counting law for two-prime primitive abundant numbers
